title: SAL-07 Sales Cycle: declared formula, numerator and denominator with honest missing-data behaviour
risk: The Sales Cycle figure is produced under different accounting rules - the median presented as the sales cycle, or the mean computed over only the orders that converted quickly - so the KPI is wrong in the direction that flatters the programme and every decision taken on it inherits the error.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.

Metric scope is fixed before measurement: numerator is closed cycles that have both a first-need timestamp and a confirmed-payment timestamp; denominator is not a ratio - a duration in hours with the censoring rule stated.
The dictionary entry for 'Sales Cycle' (owner, unit, window, exclusion rule) is loaded read-only and is compared with the recomputation instead of being trusted.

inputs.formula: mean elapsed hours between first need intake and confirmed payment
inputs.expected_value: 45 hours (mean of the eight synthetic cycles)
inputs.wrong_value_if_buggy: the median presented as the sales cycle, or the mean computed over only the orders that converted quickly
inputs.expected_boundary_behaviour: cycles still open at window end are right-censored and excluded, never counted as 0 hours

steps.action: Compute Sales Cycle from the frozen rows in kpi_dataset.sales
steps.expected: The stored aggregate reports 45 hours (mean of the eight synthetic cycles) and records the formula, the window and the currency that produced it.

steps.action: Recompute Sales Cycle independently from the raw counter rows for the same tenant and window
steps.expected: The recomputed value equals the stored value 45 hours (mean of the eight synthetic cycles), and every numerator row lies inside the denominator scope.

steps.action: Force the empty-source variant of the metric (no qualifying row in the window)
steps.expected: The metric reports cycles still open at window end are right-censored and excluded, never counted as 0 hours; the display distinguishes missing source data from a measured zero.

steps.action: Read the dashboard payload and the metric dictionary entry
steps.expected: The dashboard renders the stored value with its window, coverage and source, and the dictionary names the owner, unit, numerator and denominator that the recomputation used.

assertions: Sales Cycle equals 45 hours (mean of the eight synthetic cycles) for the frozen window, recomputed from the raw counter rows with numerator scope 'closed cycles that have both a first-need timestamp and a confirmed-payment timestamp' and denominator scope 'not a ratio - a duration in hours with the censoring rule stated'.

A recomputation that yields the median presented as the sales cycle, or the mean computed over only the orders that converted quickly is detected as wrong: the stored aggregate and the independent recomputation must agree before the figure is published.
The dashboard payload for the same tenant and window carries the stored value with its window, coverage and measurement source; it substitutes neither a design target nor another metric's value.
Boundary behaviour: cycles still open at window end are right-censored and excluded, never counted as 0 hours; missing source data is never rendered as a measured zero.
forbidden: Counting an abandoned cycle as a zero-length sale.
Reporting the cycle for only the fastest customer segment.
evidence: Cycle table with the first-need and payment timestamps.
Censoring report listing the cycles excluded at window end.
cleanup: Delete gov- aggregate, raw-counter and scenario rows for SAL-07 after exporting the recomputation table.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
